title: How to learn good representations by prediction?
reading: The slide poses the question of how prediction can yield good representations, and answers visually with a masked autoencoder example on a cheetah photograph: a heavily masked input, the model's reconstruction, and the ground-truth image, labelled Input, MAE prediction, and GT.

visuals.description: Three side-by-side images of a cheetah: left, the image with most patches greyed out (masked); centre, a blurry but structurally correct MAE reconstruction; right, the original sharp photograph. Captions: Input, MAE prediction, GT.
visuals.assertion: A masked autoencoder can reconstruct plausible global structure and semantics of an image from a small fraction of visible patches, though fine detail is blurred — evidence that predicting masked content forces useful representation learning.

concepts.name: Masked autoencoder (MAE)
concepts.why_it_matters: Self-supervised pretraining by reconstructing masked image patches.

concepts.name: Representation learning by prediction
concepts.why_it_matters: Framing motive: predicting hidden parts of data induces semantic features.
